pages.title: Page 101
pages.content:
6.5 Callbacks

Callbacks are functions you define on the global objects. The firmware calls them when things happen.

page.onInit()

Called once after the script loads and the Lua environment is ready. Use this to set the page title, initialize script state, and request data from external gear.

function page.onInit()
    page.setTitle("Synth Edit")
    midi.sendSysex(0, {0xF0, 0x7D, 0x02, 0xF7})  -- request current values
end

controller.onEncoderTurn(enc)

Called when a turn destination receives a value update, including ordinary controls as well as Script controls. A physical encoder turn is the normal source, but recorder, random, group, or other internal value processing can also produce a callback. With two destinations enabled, each destination is handled independently; with Change Destination enabled, only the active destination is handled.

For ordinary controls and managed Script controls, the callback is sent after the value is stored and only when its mapped output value changes. For manual Script controls, it is sent before any automatic value change; the script receives the currently stored value and decides whether to replace it.

The enc table contain

Field　Type　Description

enc.id　int
Script ID for a Script destination. For ordinary controls, use enc.page and enc.index to identify the control.

enc.index　int
Encoder position on the page (1–16)

enc.page　int
Current page (1–12)

enc.increment　int
Raw turn direction and speed: ±1, ±2, ±4, or ±8. This is an independent input signal, not the provenance of enc.value ; it is 0 when no physical increment is available (e.g. ongroup slave turns).

enc.value　int
Internal 14-bit value (0–16383). Newly committed in managed mode; currently stored value in manual mode.

enc.scaled　int
enc.value mapped to this destination's output range. Newly committed in managed mode; currently stored value in manual mode.

end.is_held　bool
Reserved for held-turn detection; currently always false

function controller.onEncoderTurn(enc)
    if enc.id == 1 then
    midi.sendCC(0, 1, 74, enc.scaled)
       end
end

enc.increment　int Raw turn direction and speed: ±1, ±2, ±4, or ±8. This is an independent input signal, not the provenance of enc.value ; it is 0 when no physical increment is available (e.g. ongroup slave turns).

enc.value　int Internal 14-bit value (0–16383). Newly committed in managed mode; currently stored value in manual mode.

enc.scaled　int enc.value mapped to this destination's output range. Newly committed in managed mode; currently stored value in manual mode.

end.is_held　bool Reserved for held-turn detection; currently always false

function controller.onEncoderTurn(enc) if enc.id == 1 then midi.sendCC(0, 1, 74, enc.scaled) end end

controller.onSysex(bytes)

Called when the E16 receives a SysEx message. bytes is a table of raw byte values (integers), including the 0xF0 and 0xF7 framing bytes.

function controller.onSysex(bytes)
    if bytes[2] ~= 0x7D then return end  -- check manufacturer ID
    local msg_type = bytes[3]
    if msg_type == 0x11 then
        local param = bytes[4]
        local value = bytes[5]
        -- do something with it
    end
end

page.onPageChange(previous_page, new_page)

Called when the user switches pages. Both arguments are 1-based page indices.

This is where you should clean up overlays from the previous page and set up overlays for the new page. The LED and label overlays are not automatically cleared on page change - your script manages this.

function page.onPageChange(prev, curr)
    -- Clean up
    for i = 1, 16 do
        leds.reset(i)
        slots.reset(i)
    end
    -- Set up the new page if it's one we care about
    if curr == 1 then
        for i = 1, 16 do
            slots.update(i, my_labels[i])
        end
    end
end

6.6 Control Configuration

Control Configuration

Turn destinations can be addressed in two ways: by script ID or by index. Script ID is the primary method - it addresses controls by the id from their assignment, regardless of where they are on the page. Index-based address destination 1 of a control by page and encoder position.

controller.set(id, key, value) / controller.set(id, props)

Set properties on every Script turn destination with the given Script ID. The search covers all pages and both turn destinations. If the same ID is intentionally assigned more than once, all matches are updated.

controller.set(1, "v", 8192)
controller.set(1, {l=0, h=63, n="Cutoff"})

Controller.set() updates the specified property on every turn destination with the matching Script ID.It is a direct setter, not a simulated encoder turn, so it does not trigger another callback. The v , l , h , manual , and accel properties are stored separately for each turn destination. The n property sets the encoder's shared label, so both destinations always show the same configured label

controller.setByIndex(page, index, key, value) / controller.setByIndex(page, index, props)

Set properties on turn destination 1 of a control by its page and encoder position. Use controller.set(id, ...) when the exact Script destination must be addressed, especially on controls that use destination swapping.

local pg = controller.getPage()
controller.setByIndex(pg, 1, "v", 8192)
controller.setByIndex(pg, 1, {l=0, h=127, manual=true})

6.7 MIDI Output

midi.sendCC(output, channel, cc, value)

Send a MIDI Control Change message.

- output: MIDI output port (0 = all outputs)

- channel: MIDI channel (0–15)

- cc: Controller number (0–127)

- value: Value (0–127

midi.sendCC(0, 0, 74, 64)  -- CC 74, value 64, channel 1, all outputs

midi.sendPC(output, channel, program)

Send a MIDI Program Change message.

- output: MIDI output port (0 = all outputs)

- channel: MIDI channel (0–15)

- program: Program number (0-127)

midi.sendPC(0, 0, 10)

midi.sendMidi(output, channel, status, data1, data2)

Send a generic MIDI message.

- output: MIDI output port (0 = all outputs)

- channel: MIDI channel (0–15)

- status : Complete MIDI status byte, including its channel nibble where applicable (for example, 0x90 is Note On on channel 1)

- data1 : First data byte

- data2 : Second data byte

midi.sendMidi(0, 0, 0x90, 60, 100)

midi.sendSysex(output, bytes)

Send a raw SysEx message. bytes must be a table of integers including the 0xF0 start and 0xF7 end bytes. Maximum 128 bytes per call.

midi.sendSysex(0, { 0xF0, 0x7D, 0x01, param, value, 0xF7 })

6.8 LED Rings

By default, the firmware draws LED rings based on the control’s internal value. If your script needs to show something different - quantized steps, a custom color, or a completely independent visualization - you can take over.

leds.update(index, value [, color])

Take ownership of an encoder’s LED ring and draw it.

- id: Script ID from --@assign

- value: Ring fill amount (0–16383, where 16383 = full ring)

- color: Color rotation (0–100, optional, defaults to 0)

The batch form accepts an array of {id, value [, color]} entries:

leds.update({
    {201, 8192, 10},
    {204, 4096, 4},
    {205, 12000}, -- default color 0
})

leds.updateByIndex(index, value [, color])

Update a physical encoder ring directly. index is the encoder position from 1–16. Its batch form accepts {index, value [, color]} entries:

leds.updateByIndex(15, 8192, 10)
leds.updateByIndex({
    {1, 8192, 10},
    {3, 4096, 4},
    {4, 12000},
})

Batch entries that are not tables or do not contain numeric target and value fields are ignored. Values and colors are clamped to their valid ranges.

Once either update function targets an encoder, the script owns that physical ring in the normalencoder view. It stays under script control until you call leds.reset() to hand it back. Menus and other special views may temporarily draw their own ring state. The override is not page-specific, so reset or replace it from page.onPageChange() when appropriate.

leds.reset(index)

Hand the LED ring back to the firmware. The firmware will resume drawing it from the control'sinternal value on the next render.

leds.reset(15)  -- firmware takes over encoder 15's ring again

6.9 Screen Labels

By default, each encoder shows the shared label from its control configuration (the 4-character abbreviation), including Script controls in manual mode. Your script can override this to show parameter names, values, status text, or whatever fits. Labels longer than 4 characters are truncated.

slots.update(index, text)

Override the label for a physical encoder slot. This visual override takes precedence over the label configured through the app or controller.set(id, "n", ...) until it is reset. It is not page-specific, so reset or replace it from page.onPageChange() when appropriate.

- index: Encoder position (1–16)

- text: Label text (max 4 characters displayed)

slots.update(1, "Cut")
slots.update(2, "Reso")

slots.reset(index)

Remove the override and revert to the control’s default label.

slots.reset(1)  -- shows control.abbr again

6.10 Variables

Variables are persistent script-side state. Unlike Lua locals (which are recreated whenever the script reloads) or values you keep in module-scope tables (which die when the Lua VM is destroyed on scene exit), variables are stored in flash and survive scene exits and power cycles. The user can edit them at runtime via the device’s variable menu; your script reads them with var.get.

Each variable has a name and a type — int, bool, or float — fixed at registration time. Variables exist per scene; two different scenes can both have a variable called "cutoff" without interfering.

var.register(name, type, default)

Declare a variable. The first call seeds the default value; subsequent calls with the same name are silently no-op so that re-running the script (e.g. via hot-reload) preserves whatever value is currently stored — live-coding friendly.

- name: identifier, max 16 characters

- type: "int", "bool", or "float"

- default: initial value used only on first registration

var.register("channel", "int",   1)
var.register("scale",   "float", 1.0)
var.register("muted",   "bool",  false)

If the script registers more than the per-scene capacity, additional registrations are dropped. If you re-register an existing name with a different type, the type tag is not updated - the original type wins.

var.get(name)

Read the current value. Returns the value typed appropriately (integer for int, boolean for bool, float for float). Returns nil if the name was never registered.

local ch  = var.get("channel")    -- 1
local s   = var.get("scale")      -- 1.0
local m   = var.get("muted")      -- false
local x   = var.get("nope")       -- nil

The lookup is by name and is fast enough for hot paths - names registered earlier in the same script are interned by the firmware-side store.

pages.title: Page 110
pages.contentHtml:
var.set(name, value)

Update an already-registered variable. The value is coerced according to the registered type - pass a number for int / float and a boolean (or truthy value) for bool. If the name was never registered, the call is a no-op and returns nil.

var.set does not trigger page.onVarChange — that callback only fires for firmware-side edits (e.g. via the variable menu). Script-initiated writes are silent, so handlers can call var.set without recursing.

var.set("channel", 5) var.set("scale", 1.5) var.set("muted", true)

var.delete(name)

Remove a single variable. The slot is freed; subsequent var.get(name) returns nil until the script (or firmware) re-registers it.

var.delete("channel")

var.deleteAll()

Wipe the entire variable store. Equivalent to deleting every variable.

var.deleteAll()

The store is loaded from flash before your script runs, so values registered in previous sessions are present when page.onInit is called. var.register preserves those values across reloads. Calling var.deleteAll resets the store to empty regardless of what was persisted.

NOTES

pages.title: Page 111
pages.content:
Reacting to User Edits   -   page.onVarChange(name)

When the user changes a variable from the device’s variable menu, the firmware fires page.onVarChange(name) so the script can react (refresh a label, recompute a derived value, etc.). See Callbacks for details.

Example

function page.onInit()
    var.register("channel", "int",   1)
    var.register("base_cc", "int",   20)
    var.register("scale",   "float", 1.0)
    var.register("muted",   "bool",  false)

    page.setTitle("Voices")
    refresh()
end

function refresh()
    slots.update(13, "ch:" .. var.get("channel"))
    slots.update(14, "cc:" .. var.get("base_cc"))
    slots.update(15, string.format("x%.1f", var.get("scale")))
    slots.update(16, var.get("muted") and "MUTE" or "LIVE")
end

function controller.onEncoderTurn(enc)
    if var.get("muted") then return end
    if enc.id >= 1 and enc.id <= 4 then
        local v = math.floor(enc.scaled * var.get("scale"))
        if v < 0   then v = 0   end
        if v > 127 then v = 127 end
        midi.sendCC(0, var.get("channel"), var.get("base_cc") + (enc.id - 1), v)
    end
end

function page.onVarChange(name)
    refresh()
end

6.13 Scripts onboard the E16

Scripts are loaded to the E16 using the App. There are several options onboard the E16 for working with scripts. Scripts can be assigned as the parameter type for many of the control knobs. Also variables are accessible in the scene settings along with the command to erase a script.

►Accessing the Scene Variables

1. Scenes are accessible from the main view by tapping the associated knob.

2. In control view, Hold (Knob) + tap [Shift]. This opens the control editor.

3. Select the scene tab. Hold [Shift] + tap (Knob 3), 'Scene'. The edit options also include controls with knob 1 and page with knob 2.

4. To navigate and scroll the options, turn (Knob 1). Select the 'Script Variables' option for editing press (Knob 1) then turn to change the setting. The '►' tag label indicates that the parameter is editable.

5. The variable options are displayed depending on how you registered the variable in the script: int, bool or float. For example

- SomeIntVariableName 15

- SomeFloatVariableName 0.59

- SomeBoolVariableName False

- or

- SomeIntVariableName 2059

- SomeFloatVariableName 0.02

- SomeBoolVariableName True

6. Tap [Shift] to backup the menu structure.

Scripts can be cleared from the E16 by using the Scene settings..

►Erase a Script

1. Scenes are accessible from the main view by tapping the associated knob.

2. In control view, Hold (Knob) + tap [Shift]. This opens the control editor.

3. Select the scene tab. Hold [Shift] + tap (Knob 3), 'Scene'. The edit options also include controls with knob 1 and page with knob 2.

4. To navigate and scroll the options, turn (Knob 1). Select the 'Erase Script' option and press (Knob 1) to erase.

Scripts can be cleared from the E16 by using the Scene settings..

►Erase a Script

  1. Scenes are accessible from the main view by tapping the associated knob.

  2. In control view, Hold (Knob) + tap [Shift]. This opens the control editor.

  3. Select the scene tab. Hold [Shift] + tap (Knob 3), 'Scene'. The edit options also include controls with knob 1 and page with knob 2.

  4. To navigate and scroll the options, turn (Knob 1). Select the 'Erase Script' option and press (Knob 1) to erase.

  5. Tap (Knob 3) to confirm clearing the script or (Knob 2) to exit without clearing.

  6. Tap [Shift] to backup the menu structure.

Example 1: General API

--@assign id=1 abbr="C/F" name="Coarse" desc="Coarse Tune" l=0 h=127 d=1 g=1 swap=
--@assign id=2 abbr="C/F" name="Fine" desc="Fine Tune" l=0 h=127 d=2 g=1 accel
--@assign id=3 abbr="Wave" name="Waveform" desc="Waveform Select" l=0 h=3 manual=true
--@assign id=4 abbr="Driv" name="Drive" desc="Drive Amount"
--@assign id=5 abbr="FX" name="FX Swap" desc="FX Turn" l=0 h=127 d=1 g=2
--@assign id=6 abbr="FX" name="FX Push" desc="FX Push Toggle" p=true g=2

local out = 0local waves = {"sine", "sqre", "tria", "saw"}
local wave_step = 0
local fx_on = false
local my_val = 0

function page.onInit()
    page.setTitle("Synth Edit")
    slots.update(2, waves[wave_step + 1])
end

function controller.onEncoderTurn(enc)
    if enc.id == 3
        then local prev = wave_step
        wave_step = wave_step + enc.increment
        if wave_step < 0 then wave_step = 0 end
        if wave_step > 3 then wave_step = 3 end
        if wave_step ~= prev
            then local iv = wave_step * 16383 // 3
            controller.set(enc.id, "v", iv)
            slots.update(enc.index, waves[wave_step + 1])
            leds.update(enc.id, iv)
            midi.sendSysex(out, {0xF0, 0x7D, 0x01, 2, wave_step, 0xF7})
        end
    elseif enc.id == 4 then
        my_val = my_val + enc.increment
        if my_val < 0 then my_val = 0 end
        if my_val > 127 then my_val = 127 end
        leds.update(enc.id, my_val * 16383 // 127)
        slots.update(enc.index, string.format("%3d", my_val))
        midi.sendSysex(out, {0xF0, 0x7D, 0x09, my_val, 0xF7})
    elseif enc.id == 1 then
        midi.sendSysex(out, {0xF0, 0x7D, 0x10, enc.scaled, 0xF7})
    elseif enc.id == 2 then
        midi.sendSysex(out, {0xF0, 0x7D, 0x11, enc.scaled, 0xF7})
    elseif enc.id == 5 then
        midi.sendSysex(out, {0xF0, 0x7D, 0x20, enc.scaled, 0xF7})
    end
end

pages.title: Page 117
pages.content:
function controller.onEncoderPress(enc)
    if enc.id == 6 then
        fx_on = not fx_on
        local val = fx_on and 127 or 0
        midi.sendSysex(out, {0xF0, 0x7D, 0x01, 5, val, 0xF7})
        slots.update(enc.index, fx_on and "FX.Y" or "FX.N")
    end
end

function controller.onSysex(bytes)
    if bytes[2] ~= 0x7D then return end
    local pg = controller.getPage()

    if bytes[3] == 0x11 then
        local idx = bytes[4] + 1
        local value = bytes[5]
        local internal = (value * 16383 + 63) // 127
        controller.setByIndex(pg, idx, "v", internal)
    elseif bytes[3] == 0x12 then
        for i = 1, 16 do
            if bytes[3 + i] then
                local internal = (bytes[3 + i] * 16383 + 63) // 127
                controller.setByIndex(pg, i, "v", internal)
            end
        end
    end
end

function page.onPageChange(prev, curr)
    for i = 1, 16 do
        leds.reset(i)
        slots.reset(i)
    end
end

Example 2:

This example demonstrates manual value ownership, two turn destinations sharing one Script ID, writing values into another control's destinations, destination swapping, batched LED-ring overrides, dynamic slot labels, and periodic updates.

Place the two SINE assignments on encoder 1, the two TGT assignments on encoder 2, Wr1 on encoder 3, Wr2 on encoder 4, and Rate on encoder 5.

-- Manual mode test script.

--
-- Expected behavior:

--
-- Encoder 1 drives a script-owned sine-pattern LED ring.
-- - With encoder 2 destination 1 active, encoder 3 changes encoder 2's ring;
-- encoder 4 only changes the hidden destination 2 value.
-- - Swap encoder 2. Its ring jumps to destination 2's stored value. Encoder 4
-- now changes the visible ring, while encoder 3 only changes hidden dest 1.
-- - Encoder 2's target destinations stay managed so Swap behaves normally.
-- The sine control and both writer controls are manual; Lua applies their
-- increments and writes their internal values explicitly.
-- - Encoder 5 continuously sweeps up and down from system.update(). Turning
-- it changes the sweep frequency, proving that periodic Lua polling and a
-- manual Script control can work together.

--@assign id=201 abbr="SINE" name="Manual sine action A" l=0 h=127 d=1 g=1 swap=true manual=true
--@assign id=201 abbr="SINE" name="Manual sine action B" l=0 h=127 d=2 g=1 manual=true
--@assign id=202 abbr="TGT" name="Target destination 1" l=0 h=127 d=1 g=2 swap=true
--@assign id=203 abbr="TGT" name="Target destination 2" l=0 h=127 d=2 g=2
--@assign id=204 abbr="Wr1" name="Manual writer destination 1" l=0 h=127 manual=true
--@assign id=205 abbr="Wr2" name="Manual writer destination 2" l=0 h=127 manual=true
--@assign id=209 abbr="Rate" name="Polling LED frequency" l=0 h=127 manual=true

local SINE_ID = 201
local TARGET_DEST_1_ID = 202
local TARGET_DEST_2_ID = 203
local WRITE_DEST_1_ID = 204
local WRITE_DEST_2_ID = 205
local POLL_RATE_ID = 209

local step = 512
local sine_value = 4096
local dest_1_value = 2048
local dest_2_value = 14336
local writer_1_value = dest_1_value
local writer_2_value = dest_2_value

pages.title: Page 119
pages.content:
local tau = 6.283185307179586
local led_phase = 0
local led_phase_steps = 32

local POLL_LED_INDEX = 5
local poll_page = 1
local poll_led_value = 0
local poll_led_direction = 1
local poll_rate_value = 4096
local poll_led_step = 0

local function clamp14(value)
    if value < 0 then return 0 end
    if value > 16383 then return 16383 end
    return value
end

local function advance(value, increment)
    return clamp14(value + increment * step)
end

local function to7Bit(value)
    return math.floor(value * 127 / 16383 + 0.5)
end

local function updateWriterLabel(index, writer, value)
    slots.update(index, string.format("%d%03d", writer, to7Bit(value)))
end

local function updateSineLed()
    local angle = (led_phase % led_phase_steps) * tau / led_phase_steps
    local normalized = math.sin(angle) * 0.45 + 0.5
    local ring_value = math.floor(normalized * 16383 + 0.5)
    leds.update(SINE_ID, ring_value, 10)
end

local function updatePollRate()
    -- 64..2048 per 20 ms update: roughly 0.1 Hz to 3.1 Hz.
    poll_led_step = 64 + math.floor(poll_rate_value * 4096 / 16383 + 0.5)
end

pages.title: Page 120
pages.content:
function page.onInit()
    page.setTitle("All manual")
    poll_page = controller.getPage()
    system.setUpdateRate(20)

    controller.set(SINE_ID, {n="SINE", manual=true, v=sine_value})
    controller.set(TARGET_DEST_1_ID, {v=dest_1_value})
    controller.set(TARGET_DEST_2_ID, {v=dest_2_value})
    controller.set(WRITE_DEST_1_ID, {manual=true, v=writer_1_value})
    controller.set(WRITE_DEST_2_ID, {manual=true, v=writer_2_value})
    controller.set(POLL_RATE_ID, {manual=true, v=poll_rate_value})

    updatePollRate()
    updateSineLed()
    leds.update({
        {WRITE_DEST_1_ID, writer_1_value, 4},
        {WRITE_DEST_2_ID, writer_2_value, 8},
        {POLL_RATE_ID, poll_led_value, (poll_led_step / 16383) * 100},
    })
    updateWriterLabel(3, 1, writer_1_value)
    updateWriterLabel(4, 2, writer_2_value)
end

function page.onPageChange()
    for i = 1, 16 do
        slots.reset(i)
        leds.reset(i)
    end
end

function system.update()
    if controller.getPage() ~= poll_page then return end

    poll_led_value = poll_led_value + poll_led_direction * poll_led_step
    if poll_led_value >= 16383 then
        poll_led_value = 16383
        poll_led_direction = -1
    elseif poll_led_value <= 0 then
        poll_led_value = 0
        poll_led_direction = 1
    end

    leds.update(POLL_RATE_ID, poll_led_value, (poll_led_value / 16383) * 100)
end

function controller.onEncoderTurn(enc)
 if enc.id == SINE_ID then
        sine_value = advance(sine_value, enc.increment)
        led_phase = (led_phase + enc.increment) % led_phase_steps
        controller.set(SINE_ID, "v", sine_value)
        updateSineLed()
        page.setTitle("Sine " .. sine_value)

    elseif enc.id == TARGET_DEST_1_ID then
        -- Managed target: firmware has already applied the increment.
        dest_1_value = enc.value
        page.setTitle("T1 " .. dest_1_value)

    elseif enc.id == TARGET_DEST_2_ID then
        -- Managed target: firmware has already applied the increment.
        dest_2_value = enc.value
        page.setTitle("T2 " .. dest_2_value)

    elseif enc.id == WRITE_DEST_1_ID then
        writer_1_value = advance(writer_1_value, enc.increment)
        dest_1_value = writer_1_value
        controller.set(WRITE_DEST_1_ID, "v", writer_1_value)
        controller.set(TARGET_DEST_1_ID, "v", dest_1_value)
        leds.update(WRITE_DEST_1_ID, writer_1_value, 4)
        updateWriterLabel(enc.index, 1, writer_1_value)
        page.setTitle("D1 " .. dest_1_value)

    elseif enc.id == WRITE_DEST_2_ID then
        writer_2_value = advance(writer_2_value, enc.increment)
        dest_2_value = writer_2_value
        controller.set(WRITE_DEST_2_ID, "v", writer_2_value)
        controller.set(TARGET_DEST_2_ID, "v", dest_2_value)
        leds.update(WRITE_DEST_2_ID, writer_2_value, 8)
        updateWriterLabel(enc.index, 2, writer_2_value)
        page.setTitle("D2 " .. dest_2_value)

    elseif enc.id == POLL_RATE_ID then
        poll_rate_value = advance(poll_rate_value, enc.increment)
        controller.set(POLL_RATE_ID, "v", poll_rate_value)
        updatePollRate()
        page.setTitle("Rate " .. to7Bit(poll_rate_value))
    end
end

-- Sysex address byte per script_id (1-86)
local param_num = {
    -- OP4 (1-16)
    11, 2, 1,12,  0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9,10, 4, 3,
    -- OP3 (17-32)
    24, 7, 6,25, 13,14,15,16,17,18,19,20,22,23, 9, 8,
    -- OP2 (33-48)
    37,12,11,38, 26,27,28,29,30,31,32,33,35,36,14,13,
    -- OP1 (49-64)
    50,17,16,51, 39,40,41,42,43,44,45,46,48,49,19,18,
    -- Voice common (65-81): VCED addresses
    0x34,0x35,0x36,0x37,0x38,0x39,0x3A,0x3B,
    0x3C,0x3D,0x3E,0x3F,0x40,0x41,0x42,0x47,0x48,
    -- Ratio/Fixed (82-85): ACED addresses Op4,Op3,Op2,Op1
    0x00,0x05,0x0A,0x0F,
    -- Reverb (86): ACED address
    0x14,
}

-- Operator enable state: Op1, Op2, Op3, Op4 (1=on, 0=off)
local op_en = {1, 1, 1, 1}

local function sendOpEnable()
    local packed = (op_en[1] * 8) + (op_en[2] * 4) + (op_en[3] * 2) + op_en[4]
    vced[5] = 0x5D
    vced[6] = packed
    midi.sendSysex(out, vced)
end

function page.onInit()
    page.setTitle("TX81Z")
end

function controller.onEncoderTurn(enc)
    if enc.id >= 1 and enc.id <= 86 then
        local msg = param_type[enc.id] == 1 and aced or vced
        msg[5] = param_num[enc.id]
        msg[6] = enc.scaled
        midi.sendSysex(out, msg)
    end
end

function controller.onEncoderPress(enc)
    -- Op enable toggles (id 87=OP1, 88=OP2, 89=OP3, 90=OP4)
    if enc.id >= 87 and enc.id <= 90 then
        local op = enc.id - 86  -- 1-4
        op_en[op] = 1 - op_en[op]
        sendOpEnable()
        slots.update(enc.index, op_en[op] == 1 and "ON" or "OFF")
    end
end

NOTES
